reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily provides an educational explanation of Toshi and its ecosystem while stating that it is not financial advice. The speaker presents the $200 deposit and credit example as a trading explanation, warns that the credit does not remove risk or guarantee profit, and describes meme coins as volatile and speculative. The displayed website and NFT controls provide project context and navigation, without establishing deceptive conduct.

citations.quote: in this video I'll break down what it is, how it works, and what makes it different from meme baser token
With a quick example, you deposit $200 and get an additional $200 as bound credit.
That's bringing your total equity to $400.
Toshi is a community driven meme coin built on the Base blockchain
The TOSHI token is mainly used for community participation governance, voting, access to certain ecosystem's tools

opening.argument: The trading example presents a concrete financial action paired with an immediate additional asset: viewers are told to deposit $200 and receive another $200 as credit, producing $400 in total equity. That is not merely a definition of cryptocurrency; it gives a simple deposit-to-benefit pathway that can make participation appear unusually easy. The explanation says the added margin may keep a position open longer, which makes the credit operationally attractive even though eligibility, provider, restrictions, and withdrawal conditions are not established. The warning that risk remains does not remove the inducement created by linking a deposit to doubled account equity.

citations.quote: you deposit $200 and get an additional $200 as bound credit
That's bringing your total equity to $400.
the extra margin may help your position open for a longer time

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the example educational does not answer the central issue: the video supplies a specific deposit-and-credit structure while omitting who provides it and what conditions govern it. The reference framing also treats the risk disclaimer as dispositive, but a disclaimer cannot explain whether the advertised credit is real, withdrawable, or available to viewers. The concrete $200-to-$400 presentation is more actionable than the general educational label suggests.

citations.quote: With a quick example, you deposit $200 and get an additional $200 as bound credit.
this doesn't remove risk and doesn't guarantee profit!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted example does not promise a reward for viewers or identify a registration, payment, or platform they are asked to use. It explicitly says the credit is an example, may only help a position remain open, does not remove risk, and does not guarantee profit. The video therefore explains a trading concept while expressly limiting the interpretation the prosecution places on it.

citations.quote: With a quick example, you deposit $200 and get an additional $200 as bound credit.
this doesn't remove risk and doesn't guarantee profit!
this video is for educational purposes only and not in here is financial advice

opening.argument: The presentation combines several concrete participation signals: cryptocurrency promotion, a deposit-linked credit example, an external project website, and a visible collection page with an invitation to explore it. The site also displays the identity claim “NOW ON Coinbase,” while another visible panel calls NFTOSHIS 2.0 “BASED & VERIFIED.” Those claims place authority and verification beside a route into a digital-asset collection. In that context, the disclaimer and volatility warnings do not resolve whether the affiliation or verification claim supports a legitimate destination; they can instead make the surrounding promotion appear safer while leaving the underlying offer unverified.

citations.quote: WEBSITE : https://bit.ly/nasscryptobonus
you deposit $200 and get an additional $200 as bound credit

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes the website and controls as mere context, but the displayed page pairs an apparent Coinbase affiliation with the Toshi branding, and the NFT panel pairs verification language with an “Explore the collection” control. Those are not neutral risk disclosures. The video also directs viewers to the official website, so the external destination is part of the presentation rather than incidental background.

citations.quote: If you want to explore TUSHY, visit the official website.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The frames show project navigation and branding, but they do not establish that viewers are promised a free asset, that a Coinbase endorsement is genuine, or that clicking the collection control requires payment or produces a reward. The description actually warns viewers to do research and not pay external managers. Visual presence and a navigation button are insufficient to prove a deceptive claim-action flow.

citations.quote: Do your research before deciding to invest.
NEVER pay to external managers.

opening.argument: Although framed as an explanation, the video repeatedly turns that format into a guided route toward participation. It introduces Toshi as a project viewers may explore, emphasizes its ecosystem and tools, tells interested viewers to visit the official website, and shows a collection page with an “Explore the collection” action. The result is not only neutral education: project descriptions, authority-signaling language, and destination links are arranged to move viewers from curiosity to an external digital-asset destination. The educational label and disclaimer do not change that practical promotional function.

citations.quote: One project getting attention right now is toshi
If you want to explore TUSHY, visit the official website.
LINKS OF THE PROJECT

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on what the speaker calls the video, rather than what the video does. A disclaimer can coexist with promotion; it does not negate the combination of a project spotlight, ecosystem benefits, a website destination, and a collection exploration control. Describing token uses and community involvement supplies promotional reasons to engage even if no explicit command to purchase is spoken.

citations.quote: it's combined meme culture with utility, and it has strong community involvement
If you want to explore TUSHY, visit the official website.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material shows discussion and optional further research, not a demand to click, register, deposit, or buy. The speaker repeatedly characterizes the asset as volatile and speculative, says early development does not guarantee success, and advises viewers to take their time. A project link and an exploration button do not by themselves establish a low-barrier reward or deceptive acquisition flow.
